data.long_meaning: The name Khallad means early or abundant. It is derived from the Arabic root 'kh-l-d', which means to precede, to be earlier, to go before. This name is often given to boys born before the due date, as a reminder of their early arrival.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Khallad signifies the spiritual journey of one who precedes the path, leading others to the truth and enlightenment. It is a reminder to be a trailblazer, a pioneer, and a leader in one's community.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Khallad carries the energy of the number 3, which represents creativity, self-expression, and communication. Those named Khallad are often gifted artists, writers, or communicators, and they have a natural ability to inspire and uplift others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khallad holds cultural significance in Arabic-speaking communities. It signifies the birth of a child before the due date, highlighting the family's blessings and collective joy that comes with the arrival of a new member. This early birth can also bring a sense of pride and recognition within the community, as it is viewed as a sign of God's blessings and providence.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Khallad holds deeper meanings. It can be seen as a reminder of Allah's mercy and compassion. Just as a child is brought early into the world, Allah allows people to enter this world before their appointed time as well – through Divine guidance and providence. The name, therefore, encourages believers to reflect on the fragility and fleeting nature of life, and to constantly strive for spiritual growth and development. The early arrival of a child can also serve as a reminder for parents to cherish and nurture their child, as every moment is precious and a gift from Allah.

historical_references.reference: Khallad ibn Asid was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the Ten Promised Paradise. He was known for his generosity and piety. He was born in the pre-Islamic era, around 552 CE, in the city of Khaybar in Arabia.

Khalid ibn al-Walid, also known as Sa'd ibn Rabi'ah, was a prominent military commander under the Rashidun Caliphs, Abu Bakr and Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He was one of the most successful military commanders in Islamic history. He was born around 592 CE in Mecca and converted to Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad.
